{{short description|American astrophysicist (born 1940)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2020}}

'''Rudolph E. Schild''' (born 10 January 1940) is an [[astrophysicist]] at the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics]], who has been active since the mid-1960s.<ref name=CFA-rps>{{Cite web|url=http://cfa-www.harvard.edu/~rschild/rps.html|title = Rudy's Personal Statement}}</ref> He has authored or contributed to over 250 papers, of which 150 are in refereed journals.<ref name=pub>{{Cite web|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/nph-abs_connect?author=schild,r&nr_to_return=all|title = Nasa/Ads}}</ref>

==Career==
Schild's research in the 1980s and '90s was focused on using [[gravitational lensing]] to determine the age of the universe and the [[Hubble constant]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Erickson |first=Jim |date=March 28, 1991 |title=Tracking the age of the universe |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/arizona-daily-star-tracking-the-age-of-t/131112873/ |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=September 2, 2023 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Holden |first=Constance |date=November 8, 1996 |title=Firming up a hubble constant |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/213560484 |work=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |access-date=September 2, 2023 |id={{ProQuest|213560484}} }}</ref> The investigation into quasar images also, in 1994, suggested the existence of a [[binary pair]] of stars within a few light years of Earth.<ref>{{cite news |last=Reddy |first=Francis |date=October 2005 |title=The Double Quasar |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/215922402/1271327342DD4C6BPQ |work=[[Astronomy (magazine)|Astronomy]] |access-date=September 2, 2023 |id={{ProQuest|215922402}}}}</ref> He also published in 1996 his findings on [[rogue planets]] identified through analysis of [[Hubble Space Telescope]] images.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--not stated--> |date=April 21, 1996 |title=Hubble telescope findings indicate possibility of rogue planets |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/hartford-courant-hubble-telescope-findin/131113660/ |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |access-date=September 2, 2023 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Catalano |first=Peter |date=December 1997 |title=On the trail of rogue planets |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/215924492/1271327342DD4C6BPQ |work=[[Astronomy (magazine)|Astronomy]] |access-date=September 2, 2023 |id={{ProQuest|215924492}}}}</ref> Then, in the 2000s, Schild began focusing on the double galaxy CSL-1 and [[superstring theory]], which was noted as a possible step toward uncovering the [[theory of everything]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Chown |first=Marcus |date=March 2, 2005 |title=Strung up |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-independent-strung-up-by-marcus-chow/131111970/ |work=[[The Independent]] |access-date=September 2, 2023 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Schild is a member of a group of researchers who have published frequently on the claim that photos on [[Mars]] from various NASA rover missions have shown evidence of fossilized life.<ref>{{cite news |last=Knapton |first=Sarah |date=March 6, 2023 |title=Fossil samples may be evidence of life on Mars |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-leader-post-fossil-samples-may-be-ev/131112492/ |work=[[The Leader-Post]] |access-date=September 2, 2023 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He is a proponent of "[[magnetospheric eternally collapsing object]]s" (MECOs),<ref>{{cite journal |author1=R.E. Schild |author2=D.J. Leiter |author3=S.L. Robertson |year=2006 |title=Observations Supporting the Existence of an Intrinsic Magnetic Moment inside the Central Compact Object within the Quasar Q0957+56 |journal=[[The Astronomical Journal]] |volume=132 |issue=1 |pages=420–432 |arxiv=astro-ph/0505518 |bibcode=2006AJ....132..420S |doi=10.1086/504898 |s2cid=119355221}}</ref> an alternative to [[black hole]]s.<ref name=theage>{{cite web |author=I. Sample |date=30 July 2006 |url=https://www.theage.com.au/world/us-teams-quasar-probe-sinks-black-hole-theory-20060730-ge2tgj.html |title=US team's quasar probe sinks black hole theory |work=[[The Age]] |access-date=September 2, 2023}}</ref> These results are most often published in ''[[Journal of Cosmology]]'', a fringe astronomy journal edited by Schild himself,<ref>[https://thejournalofcosmology.com/About.html Journal of Cosmology]</ref> while his other research is published in mainstream astronomy journals such as ''[[MNRAS]]'' and the ''[[Astronomical Journal]]''.<ref name=pub/>

==Personal life==
Schild is married to mezzo-soprano [[Jane Struss]], who teaches voice at [[Longy School of Music]].<ref name=CFA-rps/>
